To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of tight d functions to the XZP basis sets is essential to obtain accurate ZPVEs and atomization energies for molecules of the second-row elements.
the XZP + d and XZP+ d-DKH basis sets provide accurate ZPVEs and atomization energies for second-row compounds.

the XZP + 1d and X2P + 1D-KH basis sets provide a very reliable description of ZPVEs and atomization energies, and they can be used in conjunction with non-relativistic and Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonians.

the development and application of high-precision basis sets and computational methods for the accurate prediction of molecular properties.

the construction and application of new basis sets for the second row elements in the context of nonrelativistic, Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH) and spin-orbit coupled relativistic Hamiltonians, for use in conjunction of coupled cluster methods, and in particular, in the computation of molecular properties, such as zero-point energies (ZPEs) and atomisation energies (AEs).
the development of all-electron basis sets for the second row of elements, which are optimized for the use of the nonrelativistic, Douglas–Kroll, and Douglas–K roll–Hess Hamiltonian.
